title: Ar-Rashid, Guide to the Right Path
hookLine: the Guide to the Right Path
tomorrow: the moving truck is late, and Dadi is slow. now what?

cards: Click, click, click. The turn signal is on, the light is green, and you still haven't decided which lane. That sound is the sound of a choice being put off.

At Amira's house it's ticking too. Dadi's knee can't do stairs, and there are two ways to give her a ground-floor room: Amira's bedroom, or the little office where her dad does the coffee shop's books.
Nobody will choose for her. How does a person pick right?

teach.b: Today's Name is Ar-Rashid, the Guide to the Right Path, explained in the classical works on the Names as the One whose every decision is sound and who leads things to their right end.
The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's words: "The right direction is henceforth distinct from error." Distinct, but you still have to walk it. So the tradition walks it in steps.
First, ask. The Prophet, peace be upon him, taught his companions to seek Allah's choice in their affairs, Jabir says, the way he taught them a surah of the Qur'an.
It's called istikhara: two rak'ahs of prayer, then a du'a asking that if the matter is good, it be made easy, and if not, that it be turned away from you, and you from it.
Here's the thing to tell a friend: the hadith says nothing about waiting for a dream.
People expect a sign; the du'a asks to be steered. Second, consult.
Surah Al 'Imran: "consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah." Third, that last part. Decide, step, and trust.
Rightly guided isn't knowing the whole road. It's taking the next step well.

how: Muslims facing a decision often pray istikhara, two voluntary rak'ahs followed by the du'a taught in the hadith, and also ask advice from people they trust before deciding.

o: the Watcher who records the paths you take
the Judge who marks each choice right or wrong
the Guide whose every decision is sound

games.q: the steps to a choice — tap the pairs.
p: then put thy trust in Allah
the Guide to the Right Path

s: after istikhara, the answer comes to you in a dream
the hadith describes a prayer and a du'a asking to be steered. it says nothing about a dream.
the Qur'an pairs consulting others with trusting Allah once you've decided
"consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah."

games.q: your friend has two summer job offers and texts you: 'just pick one for me, i can't.' what fits today's lesson?
o: talk both through with her, then let her decide and trust it.
pick for her; a friend's choice saves her from the worry.
tell her to wait until something feels like a clear sign.
games.why: consulting is one of the steps, but the deciding stays hers: 'when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah.'

practice: Stand up and walk very slowly across the room and back. Feel each foot choose where to land before it takes your weight. Before you turn around, stop for one breath: that pause is the asking, and the next step is the trust.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Rashid. The Guide to the Right Path, whose every decision is sound.

orig.note: Arabic: the Guide to the Right Path, from the traditional list of the Names.

carryVoice: Something to walk with: rightly guided, one sound step at a time. Name ninety-eight, and only one to go.
